ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Passage Mass Versus Prior Mass Score for Answer Support
PROPOSAL: Generate answers with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for 1200 RAGTruth question-answering and summarization items, each paired with a passage that suffices. Calculate gradient-times-input attribution for each generated token and split its mass between passage tokens, which gives E, and the query plus earlier generated tokens, which gives I. Score an answer by I minus E and fit a one-feature logistic classifier on 800 items. Evaluate on the 400 remaining items with AUROC and precision at fixed recall.
CONTROLS: Compare with a token-probability baseline, a length-only baseline, and ReDeEP-style scores on the same split. Ablate the attribution method by swapping gradient-times-input for attention rollout, and score answers produced after the passage was shuffled.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: I minus E should reach an AUROC near 0.75, clearly above the length and probability baselines. It may fail on summarization, where supported answers still lean on phrasing priors of the model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Integrated Attribution of Retrieved Text in Generated Answers
PROPOSAL: Generate answers with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for 1200 RAGTruth items, each paired with a passage that suffices. Calculate integrated-gradients attribution for each generated token with 256 interpolation steps from three baseline embeddings, and split the mass between passage tokens, giving E, and the query plus earlier generated tokens, giving I. Score an answer by I minus E and fit a one-feature logistic classifier on 800 items. Evaluate on the other 400 items with AUROC, and re-estimate the score under five baseline embeddings to chart its spread.
CONTROLS: Compare with token-probability, length-only, and ReDeEP-style baselines on the same split. Ablate the attribution method by swapping integrated gradients for plain gradients, and score answers produced after the passage was shuffled.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: I minus E should reach an AUROC around 0.76, above the length and probability baselines. It may fail on data-to-text items, where correct answers copy fields nearly verbatim and E is high for both classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Passage-Conditioned Likelihood Gain as a Utilization Signal
PROPOSAL: Score each generated answer token under Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct twice, once with the retrieved passage and once without it, on 1500 RAGTruth items from three task types. Define E as the summed log-likelihood gain from the passage and I as the log-likelihood the tokens keep without it. Fit a logistic classifier on the pair of signals using 1000 items and test on 500. Repeat the procedure with Mistral-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to see whether the signals transfer between model families.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity-only baseline, an n-gram copy baseline against the passage, and a length baseline. Ablate the passage removal by substituting an unrelated passage drawn from another item.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The likelihood gain should separate hallucinated from supported answers with AUROC above 0.7 in all three families. It may fail on data-to-text items, where correct answers nearly copy the source and E is large for both classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Divergence Between Passage-Free and Passage-Conditioned Next-Token Laws
PROPOSAL: Run Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 1500 RAGTruth items and sample answers at twenty decoding temperatures between 0.1 and 1.5. For each sample calculate the divergence between the passage-conditioned and passage-free next-token distributions as E, and the passage-free entropy as I. Fit a gradient-boosted classifier on 1000 items, test on the other 500, and rerun the fit on thirty resamples of the training split to bound the spread of the AUROC. Report the outcome separately for each temperature.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity-only baseline, an n-gram copy baseline against the passage, and a length baseline. Ablate the divergence by substituting an unrelated passage drawn from another item.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The divergence should separate hallucinated from supported answers with an AUROC above 0.7 at low temperatures. It may fail at high temperatures, where sampling noise swamps the difference between the two distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Counterfactual Passage Edits to Test Utilization Scores
PROPOSAL: Build 600 question-answering items from public news articles in which a named entity or a number in the passage is replaced by a plausible alternative, so that a model relying on its priors answers differently from one reading the passage. Generate answers with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and calculate a score that contrasts the passage-conditioned answer likelihood with the prior-only likelihood. Check that the score rises when the answer follows the edited passage and falls when it follows the original fact. Then apply the score to RAGTruth to see whether it flags annotated hallucinations.
CONTROLS: Compare with a random-score baseline, a perplexity baseline, and a copy-overlap baseline. Ablate the edit type by separating entity edits from number edits, and test items where both the passage and the prior agree.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The score should move in the expected direction for more than 85 percent of edited items and flag RAGTruth hallucinations at an AUROC near 0.72. It may fail for numeric edits, where tokenization splits digits and dilutes the signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Passage-Reliance Probing by Contradiction Insertion Depth
PROPOSAL: Take 600 news question-answering items and insert a contradicting sentence at one of ten positions of the passage, from first to last, then generate answers with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and a Gemma instruction model. Calculate a score that contrasts the passage-conditioned answer likelihood with the prior-only likelihood, and chart it against insertion position and against passage length in bins. Check that the score tracks whether the answer follows the inserted sentence, separately for each model and bin. Then apply the score to RAGTruth to see whether it flags annotated hallucinations.
CONTROLS: Compare with a random score, a perplexity score, and a copy-overlap score on the same items. Ablate the contradicting sentence by removing it, and test it moved into the question.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The score should follow the inserted sentence for most items, with the effect fading when the insertion comes late in a long passage. It may fail for the smallest model, where answers ignore the passage whatever its content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sentence-Removal Probes of Context Dependence in Answers
PROPOSAL: Take 1000 RAGTruth answers generated by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and remove one passage sentence at a time, recording the drop in answer log-likelihood. Define E as the largest drop over sentences and I as the log-likelihood left when the whole passage is removed. Train a logistic classifier on 700 answers with E, I and their ratio, and test on 300. Check whether the classifier detects hallucinations in answers written by GPT-4o-mini and Claude outputs when the same Llama model calculates the signals.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity baseline, a self-consistency baseline based on five resampled answers, and a length baseline. Ablate sentence removal by masking tokens at random with the same removal rate.
COST: 380
PREDICTION: The classifier should reach an AUROC near 0.7 on Llama answers and lose under 0.05 on answers from other generators. It may fail on summaries, where support is spread over so many sentences that no single removal matters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Span Deletion Profiles of Retrieved Evidence
PROPOSAL: Take 1000 RAGTruth answers generated by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and delete each contiguous passage span of one to eight sentences, recording the drop in answer log-likelihood for each span. Define E as the largest drop over spans and I as the log-likelihood left when the whole passage is removed. Train a logistic classifier on 700 answers with E, I and their ratio, and test on 300. Run the same deletion profile with a second and a third scoring model to see whether the classifier agrees across scorers.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity baseline, a self-consistency baseline based on five resampled answers, and a length baseline. Ablate span deletion by masking tokens at random with the same removal rate.
COST: 380
PREDICTION: The classifier should reach an AUROC near 0.71 under each scoring model. It may fail on short passages, where only a few spans exist and the profile has little shape.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Source-Mixture Check of Utilization Signals
PROPOSAL: Construct 2000 synthetic question-answering items whose answers are known by design to come either from the passage, through facts invented for fictitious entities, or from model memory, through well-known facts with an uninformative passage. Generate answers with an eight-billion-parameter Llama instruction model and calculate E and I with the passage-removal likelihood method. Measure how well E separates the passage-sourced answers and how well I separates the recall-sourced answers, using AUROC and rank correlation with the known source mixture of blended items. Release the items and the scoring code.
CONTROLS: Compare with a copy-overlap baseline and a perplexity baseline. Ablate the passage by shuffling its sentences, and test mixed items whose answers need one fact from each source.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: E should separate invented-fact answers at AUROC above 0.9 and I should separate recall answers at about 0.85. It may fail on blended items, where one answer needs both sources and the two signals trade off.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Source-Mixture Check of Utilization Signals by Model Size
PROPOSAL: Construct 2000 synthetic question-answering items whose answers are known by design to come either from the passage, through facts invented for fictitious entities, or from model memory, through well-known facts with an uninformative passage. Generate answers with five open instruction models spanning one to seventy billion parameters and calculate E and I with the passage-removal likelihood method for each. Measure how well E and I separate their sources by AUROC and rank correlation, for each model, and fit a curve of separability against parameter count. Release the items and the scoring code.
CONTROLS: Compare with a copy-overlap score and a perplexity score for each model. Ablate the passage by shuffling its sentences, and test mixed items that need one fact from each source.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: E should separate invented-fact answers at AUROC above 0.9 for each model, with a slow rise in model size. It may fail on the smallest model, where fluent answers are rare enough that both signals are noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leave-One-Dataset-Out Detector From Utilization Features
PROPOSAL: Collect answers and annotations from RAGTruth question answering, RAGTruth summarization, and RAGTruth data-to-text, generated by Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Calculate E and I with the passage-removal likelihood method plus the answer length, and train a logistic classifier on two tasks and test on the held-out third, for each of the three splits. Compare the held-out AUROC with a classifier trained inside the same task. Report precision at fixed recall and calibration error for the three splits.
CONTROLS: Compare with a ReDeEP-style baseline tuned on the training tasks only, a perplexity baseline, and a length baseline. Ablate each of E and I in turn to see which carries the held-out signal.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Held-out AUROC should land within 0.05 of in-task AUROC, near 0.72. It may fail when summarization is held out, because its answers are longer and its hallucinations are sparser.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Generator Transfer of a Utilization-Feature Detector
PROPOSAL: Collect answers to RAGTruth question-answering items generated by six public generators from different families. Calculate E and I with the passage-removal likelihood method using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the scorer, train a logistic classifier on the answers of one generator, and test on each of the other five, giving thirty train-test cells. Compare the cross-generator AUROC with a classifier trained within the same generator, and report precision at fixed recall and calibration error for each cell.
CONTROLS: Compare with a ReDeEP-style detector tuned on one generator, a perplexity detector, and a length detector. Ablate E and I in turn to see which feature carries the transfer.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Cross-generator AUROC should stay within 0.06 of the within-generator figure, near 0.70. It may fail for generators whose answers are much shorter, where the two signals rest on few tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Utilization Scores Under Corrupted Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Take 800 RAGTruth items and degrade their passages in three ways: drop the sentence holding the answer, swap in a distractor passage on a related topic, and insert a contradicting sentence. Generate answers with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and calculate E and I with the passage-removal likelihood method. Measure how the I minus E threshold learned on clean items shifts under each degradation, and how much AUROC survives with the clean threshold versus a recalibrated one.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity baseline and a ReDeEP-style baseline under the same degradations. Ablate the degradation severity by dropping one, two, or three sentences.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: AUROC should fall from near 0.74 to about 0.62 when the key sentence is dropped, and recalibration should recover half of the loss. It may fail for contradiction inserts, where the answer follows the passage and is still labelled wrong.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Threshold Drift of Utilization Scores Under Passage Corruption
PROPOSAL: Take 800 RAGTruth items and degrade their passages along a grid of four degradations, drop the sentence holding the answer, swap in a distractor passage, insert a contradicting sentence, and truncate the passage, each at five severities, giving twenty conditions. Generate answers with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct and calculate E and I with the passage-removal likelihood method. Measure how the I minus E threshold learned on clean items shifts in each condition, and how much AUROC survives with the clean threshold versus a recalibrated one.
CONTROLS: Compare a perplexity score and a ReDeEP-style score under the same conditions. Ablate the scoring model by repeating the grid with the second model alone.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: AUROC should fall from near 0.74 to about 0.62 when the key sentence is dropped, and recalibration should recover half of the loss. It may fail for truncation, where the loss varies little with severity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling Utilization Signals Into a Small Scorer
PROPOSAL: Calculate E and I with the passage-removal likelihood method for 10000 generated answers from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct over public grounded-generation corpora. Fine-tune a 350M-parameter encoder to regress both signals from the passage, the query, and the answer text, and use its two outputs in a logistic classifier of hallucination. Evaluate on RAGTruth and on answers from a different generator, and compare scorer cost per item with the teacher calculation.
CONTROLS: Compare with the teacher signals used directly, a fine-tuned encoder trained straight on hallucination labels, and a length baseline. Ablate the regression targets by training on E alone and on I alone.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: The scorer should keep over 90 percent of the teacher AUROC at a fraction of the cost. It may fail on answers from other generators, where surface style differs from the training answers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Retrieval-Free Estimation of Utilization From Passage Rewrites
PROPOSAL: Take 10000 generated answers from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct over public grounded-generation corpora, and for each sample twelve rewrites of the passage with the same model. Rescore the answer under each rewrite, and use the spread of the log-likelihood across rewrites as E and the log-likelihood with the passage removed as I. Train a gradient-boosted classifier on 7000 answers and test on RAGTruth and on answers from a different generator. Chart scoring cost per item against the number of rewrites used.
CONTROLS: Compare with the direct passage-removal signals, a classifier trained on labels alone, and a length score. Replace rewrites by sentence shuffles and by token dropout.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: The rewrite spread should reach about 95 percent of the AUROC of direct scoring, with little gain beyond four rewrites. It may fail on answers from other generators, where surface style differs from the training answers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Utilization-Aware Fine-Tuning of a Hallucination Detector
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with low-rank adapters to classify answers as supported or hallucinated, feeding the passage, the query, and the answer, and add E and I from the passage-removal likelihood method as auxiliary regression targets. Train on 20000 synthetic and annotated items from public grounded-generation corpora and evaluate on RAGTruth and on answers from three other generators. Report AUROC, precision at fixed recall, and the correlation of the auxiliary heads with controlled copy-versus-recall items.
CONTROLS: Compare with the same detector trained on labels alone, a prompted judge based on a frozen model, and a ReDeEP-style detector. Ablate the auxiliary targets by training with E alone and with I alone.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Auxiliary targets should add about 0.03 AUROC over labels alone and improve transfer to other generators. It may fail if the auxiliary loss dominates early training and slows the label fit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pairwise Ranking of Answers by Utilization Gap
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 7B reward-style classifier on pairs of answers to the same item, where the hallucinated answer has the greater I minus E gap, built from 20000 items of public grounded-generation corpora. Train with a pairwise ranking loss for three epochs at four learning rates and two seeds, and evaluate pairwise accuracy on RAGTruth and on answers from three other generators. Read the learned score as a detector and report its AUROC and precision at fixed recall.
CONTROLS: Compare with a classifier trained with cross-entropy on labels, a prompted frozen judge, and a ReDeEP-style detector. Ablate the pairing by drawing answers at random.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Pairwise training should add about 0.03 AUROC over cross-entropy on labels and transfer better to other generators. It may fail if the gap is small for many pairs, so that the ranking loss has little signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Proxy-Scorer Detection for Answers From Bigger Generators
PROPOSAL: Generate answers for 3000 items drawn from RAGTruth and two news-summarization corpora with four open generators of seventy, thirty-two, twenty-seven, and fourteen billion parameters. Score each answer with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as a proxy that never produced it, calculating E and I by the passage-removal likelihood method. Train a logistic classifier on 2000 items and test on 1000, and report AUROC for each generator. Compare against scoring with the generator itself on a subset of 500 items.
CONTROLS: Compare with a ReDeEP-style detector restricted to the proxy, a perplexity detector, and a length detector. Ablate E and I in turn to see which carries the transfer.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Proxy scoring should keep within 0.04 AUROC of self-scoring, near 0.70. It may fail for the biggest generator, whose answers lean on knowledge the proxy lacks and so look unsupported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt-Format Sensitivity of Proxy-Scored Utilization Signals
PROPOSAL: Generate answers for 3000 items drawn from RAGTruth and two news-summarization corpora with two open generators, and present the passage to the scorer in twelve prompt formats that vary ordering, delimiters, and instructions. Score each answer with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as a proxy that never produced it, calculating E and I by the passage-removal likelihood method. Train a logistic classifier on 2000 items and test on 1000, and report AUROC for each format.
CONTROLS: Compare with a perplexity classifier and a length classifier. Ablate the format by fixing it, and by drawing it at random per item.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: AUROC should vary by under 0.03 across formats, near 0.70. It may fail for formats that place the passage after the answer, where the scorer reads the passage with the answer already in view.
